country: # --- Kent / Sussex / Hampshire / Isle of Wight

name: Camber Sands
notes: Launch only in the year-round kite zone at the eastern (Jury's Gap / Broomhill) end. Best 3 h either side of low tide; groynes and shore break near high water.

name: Greatstone (Littlestone)
notes: Huge shallow bay, works in N–NE winds when the rest of the south coast does not. Long walk at low tide; avoid ±90 min around high tide if learning.

name: Seasalter (Whitstable)
notes: Shallow estuary flats; mid to high tide, long walk at low water.

name: Minnis Bay
notes: Thanet designated kite site, flat water in northerlies. Beach closed to kites ±2 h around high tide (sea wall).

name: Shoebury East Beach
notes: Designated kite area; shallow lagoons between sandbanks at low tide, flat water, beginner friendly.

name: Frinton-on-Sea
notes: Rig on the greensward. Ride mid to low tide: at high tide the sea reaches the sea wall.

name: Felixstowe Ferry
notes: Deben river mouth: mirror-flat lagoon on the ebb and at low tide; avoid the flood (current sets into the river).

name: Kessingland
notes: Council-approved kite zone, no groynes; large shallow pool at low tide. (Lowestoft main beach: kites Sept–May only.)

name: Sea Palling
notes: Artificial offshore reefs: flat lagoons inside, punchy waves outside; strong rips at the reef gaps.

name: Brancaster
notes: National Trust beach: use the marked kite launch zone at the beach entrance. Strong tidal streams, experienced riders only.

name: Hunstanton
notes: Flat shallow water over the sandbar at low tide; do not launch between the groynes. Rare west-facing east-coast beach.

name: Cleethorpes (Humberston)
notes: Kites zoned south of the leisure centre (Thorpe Park / Humberston Fitties end). Lagoon around mid tide, beginner friendly.

name: Redcar – Majuba
notes: Main Teesside spot, WNW through N to E. Rock reefs to the east uncover at low tide.

name: Seaton Carew
notes: Shallow, flattish water in southerlies (Tees estuary side).

name: Tynemouth – Longsands
notes: Busy surf beach: keep clear of surfers and the lifeguard zone. Kiting banned at neighbouring Whitley Bay / Cullercoats.

name: Blyth – Seaton Sluice
notes: Kiters use the Seaton Sluice (south) end of the bay. Groynes and shore dump at high tide.

name: Beadnell Bay
notes: Reef break plus lagoon, best mid to high tide; local BKSA school.

name: Budle Bay
notes: Tidal lagoon: rideable from ~2 h before to a few hours after high water, chop only. Watersports zone open 1 Apr–31 Oct only (closed Nov–Mar for birds).

name: Wallasey (New Brighton)
notes: Low tide lagoon or mid tide; do not kite inside the summer swim flags. Launch by Wallasey Beach Club (Coastal Drive).

name: Hoylake – Red Rocks
notes: Nature reserve, experienced riders. Mid to high tide on neaps; no beach left on big springs, long walk at low tide.

name: West Kirby
notes: Dee estuary: kite only around high tide (no kitesurfing within 100 m of the tide line otherwise).

name: Ainsdale
notes: Only Sefton beach where kitesurfing is allowed: free council permit plus BKSA insurance required.

name: St Annes
notes: Club spot by the Beachcomber café. Launch ~2 h before high tide; no beach on big springs, long walk at low.

name: Walney Island – Earnse Bay
notes: Gently shelving, exposed to the Irish Sea; kite school on the beach.

name: Brean
notes: Huge tidal range: very long walk over sand and mud at low water.

name: Weston-super-Mare – Uphill
notes: Dedicated kite zone at the Uphill end. 10 m+ tides: ride ~3 h either side of high tide only.

name: Westward Ho!
notes: 1 Jun–30 Sep kites only in the designated sand-sports zone (right of the lifeguard hut). Best around low tide; no riding at high tide.

name: Saunton Sands
notes: Kite zone starts past the White Rock marker ~400 m down the beach. No kitesurfing in July and August.

name: Watergate Bay
notes: Marked Kitesports Zone north of the rocks. No kiting 2 h either side of high tide; keep out of the lifeguard flags in season.

name: Daymer Bay
notes: Camel estuary, sheltered from swell. Kites banned 10:00–18:00 in July–August. Ride on the flood or slack; strong ebb.

name: Perranporth (Perran Sands)
notes: Kiting banned at the Perranporth town end all year: use the Perran Sands (north) end. Exposed, rips in bigger swell.

name: Gwithian
notes: St Ives Bay. Kites off limits 10:00–18:00 from mid-July to early September and between the lifeguard flags.

name: Marazion – Long Rock
notes: Mount's Bay, beginner friendly in the prevailing SW (cross-on).

name: Bantham
notes: Avon estuary mouth opposite Bigbury. Low tide to 1–2 h before high; stay right of the RNLI flags, 50 m from swimmers/surfers.

name: Exmouth
notes: Duck Pond: flat estuary lagoon, launch from the Imperial Recreation Ground; stay west of the yellow buoys 15 Sept–31 Dec (Brent geese). Seafront: ±2 h around high tide.

name: Weymouth – Portland Harbour
notes: Flat water in most winds, any tide. Launch Ferrybridge / Hamm Beach; Portland Port permit and third-party insurance required. Fast ebb through Ferrybridge.

name: Weymouth – Overcombe
notes: Weymouth Bay: bump and jump, waves in easterlies.

name: Studland – Knoll Beach
notes: National Trust kite zone at the north end of Knoll Beach (not Shell Bay); NT permit required. Easterly-wind spot.

name: Poole Harbour – Shore Road
notes: Whitley Lake, Sandbanks: flat shallow harbour water; Poole Harbour Commissioners kite permit required. Best mid to high tide; boat traffic.

name: Avon Beach (Mudeford)
notes: Kite in the watersports area in front of the car park, never inside the summer swim zone.

name: Calshot
notes: Spit at the mouth of Southampton Water: lagoons and sheltered water, kite school on site. Ship traffic in the channel.

name: Ryde – Appley
notes: Solent shore: shallow sandbars and pools at low tide, waist deep at half tide.

name: Hayling Island
notes: Official kite beach just east of the Beachlands funfair (free, no safety cover); CBK club at the west end. Keep 2 line lengths off the shore in swim season.

name: West Wittering
notes: Private estate beach: kitesurfing for 2XS members only, year round, launch in the buoyed area; no launching at high tide.

name: Bracklesham Bay
notes: Long shallow beach, kite school; popular learning spot.

name: Littlehampton
notes: East Beach (Sea Road), BKSA school; flat knee- to waist-deep water around low tide.

name: Lancing
notes: Designated kitesports zone (beginner and advanced sections); stay out of the swim zones 1 May–30 Sept. Best 3–4 h either side of high tide.

name: Pevensey Bay
notes: Strict summer beach zoning (fines). Shingle at high tide, sand at low; bump and jump.

name: Kinmel Bay
notes: Flat water in WSW through N to NE. Council kite permit required (day or annual).

name: Llanddwyn (Newborough)
notes: Kites set up on the left-hand side of the beach only (turn left through the dunes). Any tide; boulders in places.

name: Rhosneigr
notes: Anglesey's main spot (Traeth Llydan / Crigyll): waves and big air. Rips near the river and the south end, yellow-buoyed lanes.

name: Black Rock Sands
notes: Kitesurfing allowed all year (land kiting banned Mar–Nov). Flat in light winds, small waves in strong ones.

name: Abersoch – Hell's Mouth
notes: Porth Neigwl: waves, gusty; experienced riders.

name: Borth – Ynyslas
notes: Dyfi estuary mouth: kite at high tide; strong tidal currents, no swimming.

name: Newgale
notes: Pembrokeshire's most popular kite beach, school on site. No launching at high tide.

name: Freshwater West
notes: Big surf beach with reef and strong currents: experienced riders only.

name: Tenby – South Beach
notes: Sheltered, flat; works SW round to NE, any tide.

name: Llangennith (Rhossili Bay)
notes: Zoned surf beach, most swell on Gower; respect the surf zone.

name: Rest Bay (Porthcawl)
notes: Any tide; Atlantic swell.

name: Longniddry Bents
notes: Edinburgh's main kite beach; best around low tide.

name: Pettycur Bay (Kinghorn)
notes: Best in SW; tide comes in fast, beginners at low tide only.

name: Leven
notes: One of the few east-coast spots for SW winds; shallow, beach parking.

name: Monifieth
notes: Tay estuary: SE–SW, wind accelerates in SW; flat, shallow, easy access.

name: Aberdeen Beach
notes: City beach for quick sessions: groynes, rip and onshore mess; Balmedie is usually better.

name: Balmedie
notes: Flat lagoons at low tide; rip strongest at mid tide, submerged posts at high tide.

name: Newburgh (Ythan)
notes: Ythan estuary flat water, 2–3 h either side of high tide.

name: Fraserburgh
notes: Large bay, best on the incoming tide; waves in W wind with NW swell.

name: Findhorn
notes: Seaward beach; Findhorn Bay inside is flat around high tide.

name: Nairn
notes: Shallow, beginner friendly; kite school.

name: Machrihanish
notes: Kintyre's big Atlantic beach: launch near the village in SW, at Westport in S–SE. Shore break in W–NW.

name: Barassie
notes: Troon's north bay; long, wide and flat, popular teaching spot.

name: Tiree – Gott Bay
notes: Long shallow bay: beginner, freestyle and freeride; flat water in SW.

name: Tiree – Balephetrish
notes: Reef-protected bay, flat water in most winds; big waves in N swell (experts).

name: Tiree – Balevullin
notes: Tiree's best waves; limited kite space, rips at high tide, rocks.

name: Tiree – The Maze
notes: Open to all Atlantic swell; Tiree Wave Classic venue.

name: Tiree – Balephuil
notes: Down-the-line waves in W; wind shadow at high tide.

name: Tiree – Crossapol
notes: Large easy beach; jumping in westerlies. Avoid the buoyed wreck.

name: Portstewart Strand
notes: 3 km beach break, best W–SW with small swell; strong rips.

name: Ballyholme (Bangor)
notes: Launch from the beach car park or yacht club; best in strong northerlies.

name: Strangford Lough – Newtownards
notes: Kite community at Newtownards Sailing Club; good in southerlies, patchy in northerlies. Keep clear of birds (overwintering Oct–Mar, Brent geese from late Aug).

name: Cloughey
notes: Ards Peninsula: flat water at low tide in easterlies.

name: Tyrella
notes: Dundrum Bay: small kickers to medium waves, onshore beginner friendly in S.

name: Cranfield
notes: Carlingford Lough mouth: standing depth, boat traffic.
